source.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (NeurIPS 2021)

confidence_rationale: Directly instantiates the ORACLE quadrant of GOV-INTERVENE-1's taxonomy: an interchange intervention sets a neural representation to the value it would take under a DIFFERENT, causal-model-specified input -- i.e. it imports privileged, target-correct information about what a hypothesised causal variable should contain -- and is used specifically as a verification/ceiling test of whether the representation has the causal properties of its hypothesised role, not as a naturalistic probe of ordinary behaviour. The paper's own explicit distinction between 'this representation CAN be made to behave like variable V under intervention' and 'the model NATURALLY implements the causal structure containing V' is close to a formal statement of GOV-INTERVENE-1's warning that an oracle result does not become evidence of natural/endogenous competence.
failure_signatures: The paper finds that a simpler baseline model fails to realize the hypothesised causal structure even under interchange-intervention testing, while a stronger BERT-based model succeeds on parts of it -- demonstrating that oracle-style verification is genuinely informative (it can and does fail), not merely a rubber-stamp of whatever structure is proposed; a positive interchange-intervention result is real information about achievable ceiling structure, but the paper is explicit that this establishes the network CAN be aligned to a causal model, not that it ordinarily exercises that structure unprompted.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Neural network representations are aligned with variables in a hand-specified, interpretable causal model, and interchange interventions -- setting a representation to the value it takes on a different input the causal model designates as producing a particular counterfactual value -- are used to experimentally verify whether the neural representation behaves as that causal variable would under the same counterfactual. A BERT-based model on a natural-language-inference task is found to realize parts of the causal structure this way; a simpler baseline model does not.
mapping.ree_translation: An interchange intervention is a paradigm case of GOV-INTERVENE-1's ORACLE axis: the intervention supplies a representation with a value drawn from the causal model's own privileged specification of what a correct/target state should be, rather than perturbing the system's own natural dynamics -- it establishes an achievable CEILING (can the representation, when forced into the right state, produce the right downstream behaviour) and downstream usability, exactly GOV-INTERVENE-1's description of the oracle role. The paper's own methodological caution -- that a positive interchange-intervention result verifies alignment under intervention, not endogenous exercise of that structure during ordinary forward passes -- directly supports GOV-INTERVENE-1's requirement that oracle results 'must not be silently treated as endogenous REE competence,' stated in the taxonomy's own terms almost a decade before REE's version of the rule.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The causal model here is hand-specified in advance by the experimenters from known task structure (a formal semantic parse of the NLI corpus), which is a much stronger and more literal 'oracle' than most REE diagnostic interventions would have available -- REE mechanisms typically lack an equally crisp, independently-verifiable ground-truth causal model to intervene from. The paper is also a static-inference-time analysis of a trained, frozen network, not an online, learning, recurrent agent, so nothing here speaks to how an oracle intervention interacts with REE's ongoing learning dynamics or commitment boundaries.
mapping.source_context: BERT-based and LSTM-based natural language inference models trained on the Multiply Quantified NLI (MQNLI) corpus, a synthetic dataset built from an explicit tree-structured natural-logic causal model, interchange interventions between paired inputs at intermediate representations.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed NeurIPS paper that formalised interchange interventions and directly seeded the widely-used 'causal abstraction' framework in mechanistic interpretability (distributed alignment search and successors build on this). Mapping fidelity moderate-high: the oracle/ceiling-vs-endogenous-competence distinction is stated almost in GOV-INTERVENE-1's own terms; transfer risk is non-trivial because the paper's causal model is hand-specified from known synthetic task structure, a stronger oracle condition than most REE interventions would have available.
